name: etcd disaster recovery: restore + live cutover
objective: CKA › Cluster Architecture, Installation & Configuration. The real disaster-recovery drill the exam wants but most benches skip: restore an etcd snapshot into a new data dir, then REPOINT the live etcd static pod and cut the running cluster over to the restored data. Runs on a dedicated THROWAWAY cluster ('kindlab-etcd') so a botched cutover never touches your main cluster or this dashboard. ⚠ Point kubectl at this lab's cluster: export KUBECONFIG=<repo>/.state/kindlab-etcd.kubeconfig  (next to your normal kubeconfig). Node: docker exec kindlab-etcd-control-plane.

questions.title: Restore the snapshot into a new data directory
questions.teach:
A teammate's backup lives at `/var/lib/etcd/snap.db` on the node, and the `canary` namespace was lost. First step of recovery: **restore the snapshot into a fresh data directory** (never on top of the live one) with `etcdutl snapshot restore ... --data-dir /var/lib/etcd/restored`.

**Gotcha:** etcd here is a **distroless** static pod — there is no `sh` in it, so run `etcdutl` **directly** via `kubectl exec` (no `sh -c`). Restoring writes a brand-new `member/` tree; it does not touch the running etcd yet.
questions.prompt:
On this lab's cluster (`kindlab-etcd`), the snapshot `/var/lib/etcd/snap.db` on node `kindlab-etcd-control-plane` holds the lost `canary` data. Restore it into a NEW data dir **`/var/lib/etcd/restored`** using `etcdutl` from inside the etcd pod.

First: `export KUBECONFIG=<repo>/.state/kindlab-etcd.kubeconfig`.

Target: `/var/lib/etcd/restored/member` exists on the node. (This does not change the live cluster yet — that's step 2.)
questions.hint: Point kubectl at the lab cluster: `export KUBECONFIG="$(pwd)/.state/kindlab-etcd.kubeconfig"`. Find the etcd pod: `POD=$(kubectl -n kube-system get pod -l component=etcd -o jsonpath='{.items[0].metadata.name}')`. Restore (distroless → call etcdutl directly): `kubectl -n kube-system exec $POD -- etcdutl snapshot restore /var/lib/etcd/snap.db --data-dir /var/lib/etcd/restored`.
questions.solution:
export KUBECONFIG="$(pwd)/.state/kindlab-etcd.kubeconfig"
POD=$(kubectl -n kube-system get pod -l component=etcd -o jsonpath='{.items[0].metadata.name}')

# distroless etcd has no shell — run etcdutl directly (no sh -c)
kubectl -n kube-system exec "$POD" -- etcdutl snapshot restore /var/lib/etcd/snap.db --data-dir /var/lib/etcd/restored

# the restored data now lives on the node (via the /var/lib/etcd hostPath)
docker exec kindlab-etcd-control-plane ls /var/lib/etcd/restored   # -> member
questions.eli5:
Think of etcd as the cluster's single notebook that records *everything* — every pod, namespace, and secret. A **snapshot** is a photocopy of that notebook from an earlier moment. Disaster struck: the `canary` namespace got erased from the live notebook. Luckily you have a photocopy at `/var/lib/etcd/snap.db`.

Step one of recovery is **not** to scribble the photocopy back into the live notebook (risky, and etcd is using it right now). Instead you **rebuild a brand-new notebook from the photocopy, in a new drawer**: `etcdutl snapshot restore ... --data-dir /var/lib/etcd/restored`. That creates a fresh, complete etcd data directory sitting quietly next to the live one. Nothing changes for the running cluster yet — you're just preparing the replacement.

There's one quirk: the etcd container is **distroless** — it has no shell inside. So you can't do `kubectl exec ... -- sh -c '...'`. You call the `etcdutl` program **directly**.

**Watch out for:**

- **Restore into a NEW dir** (`/var/lib/etcd/restored`), never over the live `/var/lib/etcd` — restoring on top of a running etcd corrupts it.
- **No `sh -c`** — the etcd image is distroless; run `etcdutl`/`etcdctl` directly via `kubectl exec`.
- Use **`etcdutl`** (the offline data tool) for restore, not `etcdctl` (the online client).
- This step changes **nothing** live — the cluster still has no canary until you cut over in step 2.
- Make sure your `KUBECONFIG` points at **this lab's** cluster (`kindlab-etcd`), not your main one.
questions.deepDive:
## etcd restore into a new data dir — full rundown

### Mental model
etcd restore is **two phases**: (1) rebuild a fresh data directory from a snapshot (`etcdutl snapshot restore`, offline, safe), then (2) make the live etcd *use* it (next step). This step is phase 1 only. You never restore on top of the running data dir.

### etcdctl vs etcdutl
| Tool | Role | Used for |
|---|---|---|
| `etcdctl` | **online** API client (needs endpoints + TLS) | `snapshot save`, get/put, `member list` |
| `etcdutl` | **offline** data tool (no server) | `snapshot restore`, `snapshot status`, defrag of a file |

Older docs show `ETCDCTL_API=3 etcdctl snapshot restore` — that path is deprecated; current etcd (3.5+) uses **`etcdutl snapshot restore`**.

### The command
```bash
kubectl -n kube-system exec $POD -- \
  etcdutl snapshot restore /var/lib/etcd/snap.db --data-dir /var/lib/etcd/restored
```
Optional cluster-identity flags (needed when restoring a real multi-member cluster; harmless to know):
```
  --name <member-name> \
  --initial-cluster <name>=https://<ip>:2380 \
  --initial-advertise-peer-urls https://<ip>:2380
```
`restore` writes `<data-dir>/member/{snap,wal}` — a complete, self-contained etcd store.

### Why distroless matters
The `registry.k8s.io/etcd` image is **distroless** — no `/bin/sh`. So:
```bash
kubectl exec $POD -- sh -c 'etcdutl ...'    # ❌ exec: "sh": not found
kubectl exec $POD -- etcdutl ...            # ✅ run the binary directly
```
The snapshot/restored files land under `/var/lib/etcd`, which is a **hostPath** from the node — so they persist on the node and survive the pod restart that the cutover triggers.

### Verify the restore
```bash
docker exec <node> ls /var/lib/etcd/restored/member   # snap  wal
kubectl -n kube-system exec $POD -- etcdutl snapshot status /var/lib/etcd/snap.db --write-out=table
```

### Gotchas & exam traps
- **New dir only.** Restoring into the live `/var/lib/etcd` while etcd runs corrupts it.
- **`etcdutl` for restore**, `etcdctl` for save — mixing them up is the classic trip.
- **Distroless → no `sh -c`.** Call the binary directly.
- **Restore is local/offline** — it needs no running etcd and makes no API calls; it just reads the file and writes a data dir.
- Restoring **does not** change the running cluster — don't expect the data back until the cutover.

### Quick reference
```bash
export KUBECONFIG="$(pwd)/.state/kindlab-etcd.kubeconfig"
POD=$(kubectl -n kube-system get pod -l component=etcd -o jsonpath='{.items[0].metadata.name}')
kubectl -n kube-system exec $POD -- etcdutl snapshot restore /var/lib/etcd/snap.db --data-dir /var/lib/etcd/restored
```

questions.title: Cut the live etcd over to the restored data
questions.teach:
Restoring a data dir recovers nothing until the **running etcd uses it**. etcd is a static pod defined by `/etc/kubernetes/manifests/etcd.yaml`; its `etcd-data` **volume** is a `hostPath` pointing at `/var/lib/etcd`. Repoint that `hostPath` to `/var/lib/etcd/restored` and the kubelet restarts etcd on the restored data — the cutover.

**Gotcha:** change ONLY the `etcd-data` volume's `hostPath.path` (the `path:` line). Do NOT touch the `--data-dir` flag or the `mountPath` — those stay `/var/lib/etcd` (the path *inside* the container).
questions.prompt:
Cut the live etcd on `kindlab-etcd-control-plane` over to the data you restored in step 1. Edit `/etc/kubernetes/manifests/etcd.yaml` so the **etcd-data** `hostPath.path` is `/var/lib/etcd/restored`. The kubelet restarts etcd; the `canary` namespace comes back.

Target: the manifest's etcd-data hostPath is `/var/lib/etcd/restored` AND namespace `canary` exists again (marker `keepme`).
questions.hint: On the node, edit only the volume's `path:` line (not `--data-dir`, not `mountPath`): `docker exec kindlab-etcd-control-plane sed -i -E 's#^(\s*path:\s*)/var/lib/etcd$#\1/var/lib/etcd/restored#' /etc/kubernetes/manifests/etcd.yaml`. Wait ~30s, then `kubectl get ns canary` (lab kubeconfig).
questions.solution:
N=kindlab-etcd-control-plane
# back up the manifest first
docker exec $N cp /etc/kubernetes/manifests/etcd.yaml /tmp/etcd.yaml.bak

# repoint ONLY the etcd-data hostPath (the 'path:' line equal to /var/lib/etcd)
docker exec $N sed -i -E 's#^(\s*path:\s*)/var/lib/etcd$#\1/var/lib/etcd/restored#' /etc/kubernetes/manifests/etcd.yaml
docker exec $N grep -nE 'path:|--data-dir' /etc/kubernetes/manifests/etcd.yaml   # only the hostPath changed

# kubelet restarts etcd on the restored data; the canary returns
export KUBECONFIG="$(pwd)/.state/kindlab-etcd.kubeconfig"
kubectl get ns canary -w     # becomes Active in ~30s
kubectl -n canary get configmap canary -o jsonpath='{.data.marker}'; echo   # keepme

verification.description: live etcd cut over to the restored data — canary recovered

questions.eli5:
You've rebuilt the notebook from the photocopy and set it in a new drawer (`/var/lib/etcd/restored`). But the clerk (etcd) is still reading the OLD, broken notebook — so the canary is still missing. The **cutover** is telling the clerk: *"stop using the old drawer, use the new one."*

How? etcd is started by the node's kitchen manager (the kubelet) from a recipe card, `/etc/kubernetes/manifests/etcd.yaml`. That card says "the data drawer is the node folder `/var/lib/etcd`" (a **hostPath**). You edit the card so the drawer is now `/var/lib/etcd/restored`. The moment you save, the kubelet notices the card changed, restarts etcd, and the clerk starts reading your restored notebook — the canary namespace reappears within ~30 seconds.

The delicate bit: the recipe card mentions `/var/lib/etcd` in **three** places — the `--data-dir` flag, the container's `mountPath`, and the volume's `hostPath.path`. You only change the **last one** (the hostPath on the node). The other two describe the path *inside* the container and must stay as-is.

**Watch out for:**

- **Edit only the `etcd-data` volume's `path:` line.** Leaving `--data-dir` and `mountPath` as `/var/lib/etcd` is correct — those are the in-container path; the hostPath is what maps to the restored data on the node.
- **No `vi` on the node** — use `sed` (the `sed` targets the exact `path: /var/lib/etcd` line).
- **Give the kubelet ~30s** to notice the manifest change and restart etcd; the API blips briefly as etcd restarts.
- If the apiserver doesn't come back, you likely edited the wrong line — restore the backup: `cp /tmp/etcd.yaml.bak .../etcd.yaml`.
- This is why the lab is on a **throwaway cluster** — a bad etcd cutover takes the whole control plane down.
questions.deepDive:
## etcd live cutover (repoint the static pod) — full rundown

### Mental model
A restored data dir is inert until the running etcd points at it. etcd runs as a **static pod** (`/etc/kubernetes/manifests/etcd.yaml`), and its data comes from a **hostPath volume** named `etcd-data`. Repointing that hostPath from `/var/lib/etcd` to `/var/lib/etcd/restored` and letting the kubelet restart the pod **is** the cutover.

### The three places `/var/lib/etcd` appears (change ONE)
| Where | Line | Change? |
|---|---|---|
| etcd flag | `--data-dir=/var/lib/etcd` | ❌ no — path *inside* the container |
| volumeMount | `mountPath: /var/lib/etcd` (name: etcd-data) | ❌ no — mount point in the container |
| **volume** | `hostPath: { path: /var/lib/etcd }` (name: etcd-data) | ✅ **yes** → `/var/lib/etcd/restored` |

The container always sees its data at `/var/lib/etcd` (the `--data-dir`/`mountPath`); you're only changing which **node directory** is mounted there.

### The cutover
```bash
N=kindlab-etcd-control-plane
docker exec $N cp /etc/kubernetes/manifests/etcd.yaml /tmp/etcd.yaml.bak   # always back up first
# repoint ONLY the hostPath path line that equals /var/lib/etcd
docker exec $N sed -i -E 's#^(\s*path:\s*)/var/lib/etcd$#\1/var/lib/etcd/restored#' \
  /etc/kubernetes/manifests/etcd.yaml
```
The kubelet watches the manifest; a content change makes it **recreate the etcd static pod** (~15-30s). etcd starts on the restored data; the apiserver reconnects; recovered objects (the `canary`) reappear.

### Verify
```bash
docker exec $N grep -nE 'path:|--data-dir' /etc/kubernetes/manifests/etcd.yaml
kubectl get ns canary                                   # Active again
kubectl -n canary get cm canary -o jsonpath='{.data.marker}'   # keepme
```

### Real-cluster notes (beyond kind)
- **Stacked etcd (kubeadm):** same idea — restore, then repoint the static-pod hostPath. Some runbooks instead restore *into* the original dir after moving it aside; repointing is cleaner and reversible.
- **Multi-member etcd:** restore on every member with matching `--initial-cluster`/peer URLs, then start them together. Single-node (kind/most exams) skips that.
- **External etcd:** stop etcd, restore the data dir, start it — no static pod involved.

### Gotchas & exam traps
- **Only the hostPath `path:` changes.** Touching `--data-dir` or `mountPath` breaks the mount.
- **Back up the manifest** (`cp`) before editing — a typo takes the apiserver down.
- **Patience:** the API blips while etcd restarts; wait ~30s before declaring failure.
- **Recovery:** if the control plane doesn't return, `cp /tmp/etcd.yaml.bak` back and wait.
- **Permissions/SELinux** on real nodes: the restored dir must be readable by etcd (uid in the pod) — not an issue on kind, but a real-world gotcha.

### Quick reference
```bash
N=kindlab-etcd-control-plane
docker exec $N cp /etc/kubernetes/manifests/etcd.yaml /tmp/etcd.yaml.bak
docker exec $N sed -i -E 's#^(\s*path:\s*)/var/lib/etcd$#\1/var/lib/etcd/restored#' /etc/kubernetes/manifests/etcd.yaml
kubectl get ns canary -w     # canary returns in ~30s
```
